A lot of people are dumping all sorts of "tweak scripts" and really don't go into the benefits of it all. I posted this on reddit in response to someone who wanted to know what changes I had made and decided to share here as well.

First, the useful shit...

Some comparison screens showing the effect some of these have on CPU and networking:
http://imgur.com/a/iTd10

Most of the reg tweaks I use:
http://pastebin.com/dLJtXmFk

Disabling scheduled tasks and some other minor things:
http://pastebin.com/24txUjkM

How my services look:
http://i.imgur.com/DOcEKm6.png

Obviously from the comparison screenshots, there is a HUGE reduction in network traffic and cpu usage. Memory reduction, not so much, but who cares? Not me. The amount of processes running is obviously reduced since I've disabled things I don't use.

Firstly, I am running Windows 10 LTSB N. LTSB is basically an enterprise version of Windows that has all the "modern" app stuff stripped out by default. That's how I like it. I see a lot of people ripping out the modern apps themselves, I decided to just skip that and let MS do it for me. My start menu is simple and dumb, just the way I like it.

This is for a desktop system on a small network with dhcp and dns enabled. I do not share nor do I ever intend to share files from this machine to any other computer on my network. It is able to access files from my Windows 2008 file server just fine. So these changes do not break the ability to access shares on the network. Windows Update functions fine as well. Not much to say about that.

I've tried to comment most of the things, yes, some of these changes overlap with what's in some of the tweak scripts and stuff floating around, but a lot of it is just me running Regshot while changing group policies (because I'm too lazy to back up my GPO files).

To anyone saying the default is fine and we shouldn't go messing around with stuff... cool. That's your thing, this is mine. I'm just sharing in case someone wanted to see what effect some of these changes have on the system itself. Maybe it'll spur some interesting discussion, maybe it'll inspire someone to dig deeper.

Other useful programs:
* Wireshark
* Process Monitor (from sysinternals)

Enough of most psychadelics will do it. LSD, shrooms, aya, 2c range. If you're new to drugs have a sober person around spot/help you. Remember set and setting, where you are internally and externally - eg calm of heart and in a forest. Read some advice from some of the more famous trippers - watts, mckenna, rogan (IMO).

/u/TimTamSlam hit the nail on the head.

Psychedelics are amazing drugs but you really need a safe, calm space to try them with an extremely trustworthy, completely sober friend on hand to look after you. Preferably somebody that is experienced in the art of tripping so they can help if things go badly.

A bad trip can scar you for life but get it right and it's incredibly enlightening. You need to be in a sound state of mind to begin with to lessen the risk of a horrifying trip though.

In my experience, the most gentle of the psychs are peyote tea followed by magic mushrooms. You shouldn't end up with what can be a horrible chemical comedown afterward and they're less likely to cause a bad trip.

If you really, truly want to see inside yourself? LSD is good but Ayahuasca is better (although incredibly hard to get hold of in most places, you usually need to travel).

Regardless of what you take, it can be a good idea to have some weed on hand afterward for the comedown as it helps to lessen any symptoms. You also need to make sure your "babysitter" gets you to drink plenty of water. Dehydration can really screw you over when it comes to mind-altering substances!

I highly recommend trying them if you ever have the opportunity to do so safely. Please don't underestimate the potential negative sides of these trips. A safe, calm place that you know and feel comfortable in paired with an experienced, sober babysitter is an absolute must, especially if you've never done it before!!
